questions.q: Why does the Dash necking process eliminate dislocations from a Czochralski seed crystal?
options: The high temperature of the melt anneals the dislocations out of the seed before growth begins
Growing a thin (~3 mm) neck at several mm/min lets dislocations, which glide on {111} planes inclined to the <100> axis, reach the free surface and exit before the crystal carries them along
The neck is grown under a strong magnetic field that pins dislocations in the seed holder
Dislocations cannot exist in silicon below a critical diameter of about 5 mm
questions.explanation: Dash's method is geometric: in a thin, fast-grown neck every dislocation inclined to the growth axis glides out to the surface within a few tens of millimetres, and the vacancy supersaturation from fast growth helps them climb out. After that the crystal stays dislocation-free unless a new one is nucleated.

questions.q: A 300 mm CZ ingot is grown from a 400 kg boron-doped melt with k = 0.8, targeted at 10 ohm-cm at the seed end. According to the Scheil equation, what happens to the resistivity toward the tail, and why?
options: It rises, because boron evaporates from the melt during the run
It stays exactly constant, because the melt is well mixed
It falls to roughly 6 to 7 ohm-cm at 90% solidified, because k < 1 leaves the melt progressively enriched in boron and C_s = k C0 (1-g)^(k-1)
It falls by a factor of about 4.5, the same as phosphorus
questions.explanation: With k = 0.8 the exponent (k-1) is -0.2, so the solid concentration at g = 0.9 is 0.1^(-0.2) = 1.58 times the seed-end value, taking ~10 ohm-cm down to ~6.4 ohm-cm. Phosphorus (k = 0.35) would give a factor of ~4.5, which is why n-type CZ ingots have a much larger axial spread.

questions.q: In Voronkov's v/G theory, what determines whether a CZ crystal becomes vacancy-rich (forming COP voids) or interstitial-rich (forming dislocation loops)?
options: The oxygen concentration: above 12 ppma the crystal is vacancy-rich

The ratio of pull rate v to the axial temperature gradient G at the interface; above a critical value of about 1.3 to 2 x 10^-3 cm^2/(min K) vacancies are swept in faster than the faster-diffusing interstitials can annihilate them
The crucible rotation rate, which sets the convective flux of interstitials to the interface
The dopant type: boron-doped crystals are always vacancy-rich
questions.explanation: Both point defects are incorporated at equilibrium and then annihilate, diffuse, and are advected at speed v. High v/G favours advection and leaves excess vacancies (COPs); low v/G gives diffusion time and the faster interstitials win. Because G is higher at the crystal edge, one pull rate can give both regimes across the radius, separated by the OSF ring.

questions.q: Why are the interstitial oxygen levels of 10 to 14 ppma found in CZ silicon deliberately retained in most logic and memory substrates rather than minimised?
options: Oxygen is an n-type dopant that sets the substrate resistivity
Oxygen cannot be removed because it comes from the argon atmosphere
Dissolved oxygen strengthens the wafer against slip during thermal processing, and controlled oxygen precipitation in the bulk provides intrinsic gettering of metals beneath a denuded zone
Oxygen lowers the melting point of the melt so pulling can proceed at a lower heater power
questions.explanation: Oxygen from crucible dissolution pins dislocations (raising yield stress) and, via a denuded-zone / precipitation anneal sequence, forms SiO2 precipitates and punched-out loops in the bulk that trap Fe, Cu and Ni. Only image sensors, power and RF products specify low oxygen, using MCZ or FZ.

questions.q: A 300 kg ingot hangs from a 3 mm Dash neck. Roughly what tensile stress does the neck carry, and what does the industry do about it at 300 mm?
options: About 4 MPa, which is negligible, so no special measures are needed
About 40 MPa, handled by using a steel seed holder
About 400 MPa, so pullers use thicker fast-grown necks, heavily boron-doped neck-less seeds, or mechanical crystal-support jaws that grip the crown after it is grown
About 4 GPa, which is why 300 mm ingots are limited to 100 kg
questions.explanation: Stress = m g / (pi r^2) = 2,943 N / 7.07 x 10^-6 m^2, about 416 MPa, uncomfortably close to practical limits for a real neck with surface flaws. Crystal support mechanisms, thicker necks and hardened (B > 10^19) seeds are the production solutions.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes Float Zone silicon relative to Czochralski silicon?
options: FZ uses a synthetic quartz crucible with a stronger magnetic field, giving lower oxygen and 300 mm capability

FZ has no crucible, so oxygen is below ~10^16 cm^-3 and resistivity can exceed 10^4 ohm-cm, but surface-tension support of the molten zone limits production diameter to 200 mm and the oxygen-free wafers are mechanically weaker in the fab
FZ is cheaper than CZ because it needs no crucible, and is used for all DRAM substrates
FZ crystals are polycrystalline and used only for solar cells
questions.explanation: In FZ an RF coil melts a short zone in a vertical poly rod, held by surface tension and electromagnetic pressure, with no container to leach oxygen. It serves power devices, detectors and high-resistivity RF substrates, at a price multiple of CZ and with a 200 mm production ceiling.
